name: Kenaz
overview: Kenaz was a male Edomite chief known primarily as the son of Eliphaz. His leadership role among the Edomites is noted in the book of Genesis, emphasizing his significance within this tribe. Scripture highlights his position without additional personal details.
namesAndTitles: The name Kenaz means 'hunting,' reflecting a proper name of Hebrew origin. This meaning offers insight into the character or heritage associated with his name, although it was not given directly by God.
familyAndRelationships: Kenaz was the son of Eliphaz, establishing a direct paternal relationship as recorded in Genesis. He is also inferred to be an ancestor of Jephunneh, connecting him to later biblical figures, though this is not explicitly stated in the text.
scriptureSignificance: Kenaz's importance in the biblical narrative stems from his role as a chief of Edom and his lineage as the son of Eliphaz. This places him within the broader context of Edomite leadership and genealogy, which is significant for understanding the historical and tribal dynamics referenced in Scripture. His connection to Jephunneh further links him to Israelite history, underscoring the interconnectedness of biblical genealogies.
